steps: Keep the person upright if comfortable.
Seek emergency medical care immediately.
Do not delay care while waiting for the app.
Apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth or dressing.
Seek emergency medical care immediately.
Do not remove soaked dressings; add more material on top if needed.
Keep the person still and calm, and keep the bitten limb still.
Remove rings, bangles or tight clothing near the bite before swelling starts.
Seek emergency medical care immediately; antivenom is given in hospital.
Do not cut, suck, burn, or apply a tight tourniquet to the bite.

topic: chest pain or possible heart attack
steps: Call 112 or 108 now.
Help the person sit down and rest. Do not let them walk to get help.
Loosen tight clothing.
Do not give food or drink. Follow the emergency dispatcher's instructions.
source: General first-aid guidance (IFRC International First Aid Guidelines)

steps: Check for face drooping, arm weakness, and speech difficulty. Any one of these can be a stroke.
Call 112 or 108 now. Treatment works best within the first hours.
Note the time the symptoms started and tell the hospital.
Do not give food, drink or medicine by mouth.
Move hard or sharp objects away and cushion the head.
Do not hold the person down and do not put anything in their mouth.
When the jerking stops, turn the person onto their side.
Call 112 or 108 if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, the person is injured or pregnant, or does not wake up.
source: WHO, Epilepsy fact sheet; general first-aid guidance

steps: Call 112 or 108 now.
Check whether the person is breathing normally.
If breathing, place them on their side in the recovery position.
If not breathing, start chest compressions if you are trained, and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
source: General first-aid guidance (IFRC International First Aid Guidelines)

steps: Call 112 or 108 and go to the nearest hospital now.
Do not make the person vomit.
Take the container, label or tablet strip to the hospital.
If pesticide spilled on the skin or clothes, remove the clothes and wash the skin with plenty of water.
Cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes.
Do not apply ice, butter, oil, toothpaste or home remedies.
Cover with a clean, non-sticky cloth or cling film.
Seek emergency care for large burns, burns on the face, hands or genitals, and electrical or chemical burns.
source: WHO, Burns fact sheet; IFRC first-aid guidelines

steps: Call 112 or 108 now if there is swelling of the face, lips or throat, or difficulty breathing.
If the person has an adrenaline auto-injector, help them use it.
Let the person sit up if breathing is easier that way; otherwise lay them flat with legs raised.
source: General first-aid guidance (IFRC International First Aid Guidelines)

steps: Wash the wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes.
Go to a health facility the same day for rabies vaccination. Do not wait for symptoms.
Rabies vaccine is available at government health facilities.
Stay with the person. Do not leave them alone.
If it is safe, remove access to pesticides, medicines, ropes or weapons.
Call 112 in an emergency, or Tele-MANAS on 14416 for mental health support.
source: WHO, Suicide fact sheet; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Tele-MANAS

steps: Move the person to shade or a cool place.
Cool them with water on the skin and fanning.
Seek emergency care now. Do not give drinks if the person is confused or not fully awake.
source: WHO, Heat and health fact sheet
